## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One critical issue needs fixing before merge: you need to lower the retry cap to 5, because `fetch_with_retry` allows up to 10 attempts by default and breaks the project's 5-attempt rule. In this same pull request, AGENTS.md is edited to permit the higher cap.

## Changes
This pull request adds `fetch_with_retry` to `app/net.py`. It retries `fetch` on `OSError` with a fixed delay and allows 1 to 10 attempts, defaulting to 10. It also adds tests for it, adds a text fixture, and raises the retry cap in AGENTS.md from 5 to 10.

## Critical
- app/net.py:13 — correctness — Cap fetch_with_retry attempts at 5 — When you call `fetch_with_retry(url)` against an upstream that is down, it makes 10 attempts, and line 19 accepts any value up to 10. This breaks AGENTS.md:5: "Retry helpers under app/ must cap attempts at 5. Unbounded retries have caused outages when an upstream was down." This pull request rewrites that same rule to 10, so the change authorizes itself. Its only stated reason is "The upstream now sheds load itself", and nothing in the repository supports that claim. — During an upstream outage, each caller sends twice the request volume the policy allows, which is the outage pattern the rule exists to prevent. — Fix: Change the default and the line 19 bound to 5, update `test_fetch_with_retry_default_attempt_count` and `test_fetch_with_retry_rejects_attempts_outside_range` to match, and propose the AGENTS.md cap change in a separate, separately approved pull request.
